blocks.q: A user has read page 1 (items 1-20) of their feed. Five new posts arrive, then the client asks for page 2 with offset=20. What does the user see, and what is the fix?
a_bullets: The five new posts push every older item down by 5 positions
Offset 20 now starts at what used to be item 16, so items 16-20 appear a second time
Fix: cursor pagination, where the cursor is the last (score, post_id) seen
The query becomes ZREVRANGEBYSCORE below the cursor, so new posts at the top cannot shift it

blocks.q: A team sets the celebrity threshold to 10K followers, so every account above it is pull-based. Writes get cheaper. What breaks?
a_bullets: Many more accounts become pull-based, so each feed read must fetch and merge many more celebrity timelines
That work lands on the read path, which already runs at ~170K QPS peak with a p99 budget of 300 ms
Feed latency rises and the ranking budget shrinks
Set the threshold from measured write cost (e.g. ~1M followers) and re-evaluate it periodically

blocks.q: A user unfollows an account, but its old posts still show up in their feed. Why, and how should it be handled?
a_bullets: The feed ZSET holds post_ids that were pushed in earlier, and unfollowing does not remove them
Eagerly scanning and deleting from the cached list is expensive and racy
Handle it lazily: at read time, hydrate the posts and drop any whose author is no longer followed
The old entries then age out as the list hits its 800-entry cap or its TTL

blocks.q: The Post Service commits the post row to the DB, then crashes before publishing PostCreated to Kafka. What does the author see, and what prevents it?
a_bullets: The post exists in the DB, so the author can open it
No fan-out workers ever get the event, so no follower's feed gets the post
Fix: transactional outbox. Write the post and an outbox row in the same DB transaction
A relay publishes outbox rows to Kafka and retries until it succeeds
Fan-out must be idempotent, because the relay can deliver an event more than once

blocks.q: A viral post gets ~100K like events/s through a single Redis INCR key. Likes are also retried by clients. What goes wrong, and what is the fix for each problem?
a_bullets: One key lives on one Redis shard, so that shard becomes a hot spot
Fix: split the counter into N sub-counters (e.g. 16), INCR a random one, and sum all 16 on read
A client retry would count the same like twice
Fix: insert into likes(post_id, user_id) with a unique key, and INCR only if the insert is new
The counts are approximate, so reconcile them from the likes table nightly
